summary: Vice Chair Philip N. Jefferson delivered an economic outlook speech covering three main topics: (1) Economic Activity - GDP grew ~2% in 2025, expected similar pace in 2026 with high uncertainty; AI infrastructure investment and deregulation may support growth; Middle East conflict poses headwind through energy prices. (2) Inflation - PCE at 2.8% headline and 3.0% core as of Feb 2026; progress stalled over past year due to tariffs; energy prices adding upward pressure; commitment to 2% target. (3) Labor Market - Showing signs of stabilization after gradual cooling in 2025; unemployment at 4.3% as of March; job growth averaging ~70k/month in Q1 2026; described as 'low-hire, low-fire' environment.
why_it_matters: Fed official signals dual-mandate risks on both sides - labor market cooling but still near natural rate, inflation above target with recent energy price pressures. Trade policy uncertainty and geopolitical tensions identified as upside inflation risks. Deregulation and AI investment cited as potential growth tailwinds.
macro_context: Speech given ~19 days before record date; represents current Fed thinking from a key policymaker. Dual mandate balance is central theme - risks to both employment and price stability. Tariffs identified as primary driver of stalled disinflation. Natural rate unemployment estimated near current 4.3% level.
